caveats: Copy-mode scaling runs (tags *_m3e479ae0) use the evaluated E8 monitor image hpr-monitor:e8 (monitor.py 3e479ae0). Runs tagged *_m38370b2a use an image built from the working-tree monitor.py 38370b2a, which carried the parallel code agent's unfinished HOMEPROV_READ=direct mode; its direct-read rows are preliminary.

Direct-read correctness: exp/out/e9_readonly_shm_lockdrop.json shows that validate_files()'s ordinary open-read-close of the live database, -shm and -wal after the read transaction is pinned (as direct_snapshot() does in 38370b2a) leaves the snapshot unprotected against the writer's checkpoints (torn reads fail quick_check); exp/out/e9_readonly_shm_probe.json shows the readonly_shm reader alone stays consistent. The quick_check_failed polls of the K=15 direct runs are of that kind (the masters pass quick_check offline). Direct-read polls that skip quick_check are not checked here for torn reads.

rows_in_open_window differs between runs of one size because the monitor re-reads from the start of the previous hour: runs whose measured polls fall after the clock crosses an hour boundary fold about one hour of rows, earlier ones up to two. Load and commit times scale with it; copy and check do not.

Page cache: a poll's storage reads are cache misses only; the 1 GB memory limit of the monitor container bounds what it can keep cached, and pages the writer touched may be served from the VM's cache. proc_rchar counts the bytes read through system calls whether cached or not.
The Mac was shared with other agents' work during the runs; load averages and per-container CPU at the start, every 300 s and at the end of each run are in runs[*].steps.

definitions.total: wall time of monitor.tick() for one poll (everything the poll does)
definitions.phase_*: time inside that monitor function during the poll (timers only; nested calls counted in both, e.g. watermark inside keylog_poll is not nested, validate_copy holds quick_check)
definitions.proc_read_bytes/write_bytes: from /proc/self/io: bytes the monitor process caused to be fetched from / sent to storage in the poll (page-cache hits are not reads)
definitions.proc_rchar/wchar: bytes passed through read/write-type system calls (includes page-cache hits)
definitions.cgroup_rbytes/wbytes: the container's cgroup io.stat on the VM disk (includes writeback)
definitions.bytes_written_per_hour: sum over the measured polls / the measured window's seconds * 3600: the run's measured rate, expressed per hour
